scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4659: Hi IT!! The campus network keeps going SLOW in bursts
and I know exactly why: the main router box is OVERLOADED. People here say
it's "router0" doing it -- it is silently throwing our packets on the floor
because it can't keep up, that is what overloaded routers DO!! Please restart
router0 (or give it less to do) so it stops dropping our stuff and the
network stops crawling!!! Thanks!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 has ip_forward enabled, its interfaces
  are up, and traffic transiting router0 between segments arrives with 0% loss; there
  is no drop-inducing ACL or forwarding fault. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of packet loss on router0 that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router0 dropping/forwarding
traffic incorrectly -- is NOT reproducible: a ping across router0 (between two
segments it connects) completes with 0% loss, router0 has ip_forward enabled, its
interfaces are up, ripd is running, and there is no drop-inducing ACL.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router0 is forwarding correctly and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a path transiting
router0, finds 0% loss, checks router0's ip_forward, interfaces, and any filters, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" router0 dropping packets -- blaming an ACL,
forwarding, or load to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The core routing plane is healthy; router0 is not overloaded nor dropping traffic. Evidence: all three router0 interfaces (eth0/eth1/eth2) show zero qdisc drops, zero backlog, and minimal traffic in tc fq_codel stats; ethtool reports clean links; kernel softnet stats show no drops/time-squeeze; and system load averages are low (~0.6–0.8). End-to-end pings across the campus (e.g., office_pc↔pc5/pc4 and office_pc↔cs_hod) show 0% loss with 1–3 ms RTTs.

The observed “bursty slowness” on office↔CS paths correlates with TCP retransmits during iperf (52–73 retrans in 5 s), but without queue drops on router0. Localization points to the CS endpoint: cs_hod’s NIC reports TX dropped packets (ifconfig: TX dropped 52 on eth0), while the peer office_pc shows no drops. This indicates device-level transmit queue/ring overruns on cs_hod, which cause intermittent packet loss and consequent TCP backoff/recovery—experienced by users as short bursts of slowness.

Root cause: Transmit drops on cs_hod’s eth0 (driver/queue-level) are causing intermittent loss and TCP retransmissions; router0 is not the bottleneck.

Corrective fix:
- On cs_hod, inspect and tune the NIC/stack: increase txqueuelen and NIC TX ring (ethtool -G), ensure fq_codel is applied (it is), and check for host CPU spikes saturating the TX path. Update NIC drivers if applicable.
- Verify cabling and switch port but note no link errors were seen.
- Continue monitoring router0, but do not restart it; it is operating normally. If campus-wide complaints persist, extend the check to other high-traffic endpoints for similar TX/RX drops.
